messages.subject: Re: [problems] Installing [R]stan
parts:
I'm cc-ing our users list, where our developers who understand
the vagaries of R can help.

It looks like there's something going wrong with your
C++ compiler and the way R's trying to call it.

I have no idea if that's a problem with our install script,
your version of Rcpp, something in your R makevars that got changed,
or what. You may need to re-install R, but I'm not sure.

If you type

> clang++ --version

and

> g++ --version

from a terminal, what do you see?

- Bob

> On Wed, Oct 15, 2014 at 4:43 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> I'm on version 10.9. We support 10.7, 10.8 and 10.9,
> but not 10.6. I'm not even sure it's possible to run
> Stan on Mac OS 10.6.
>
> I'm also pretty sure we need a later version of the
> C++ compilers than are available in Xcode 3. The
> new versions are much faster, by the way, both to compile
> and to run.
>
> Is there some reason you can't update your OS?
> I don't think you can update Xcode to the latest

>

> modern Linux server somewhere to run on? Otherwise, you
> probably need to dig down and install a C++ compiler
